summary.headline: Anup Engineering Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue of INR125 crore and EBITDA of INR9.2 crore; FY27 guidance set at 5-10% revenue growth and about 15% EBITDA margin.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue of INR125 crore was in line with management's plan but reflected a delayed execution start and supply chain issues, with revenue recognition deferred because milestones were not reached. EBITDA of INR9.2 crore reflected under-absorption of fixed costs on the low revenue base. Management said the pending order book stands at INR985 crore, with INR538 crore of new orders booked since April, and gave FY27 guidance for the first time since the prior call. Revenue is expected to be back-end loaded, with Q3 and Q4 the strongest quarters.

financial_highlights.change: In line with management plan; no YoY comparison stated
No YoY comparison stated; attributed to lower revenue and fixed cost absorption
Down from INR221 lakh in Q4 FY26; management said Q1 FY26 was about INR80-87 lakh (figure disputed on call)
Long-term debt about INR44 crore; net cash about INR1 crore

financial_highlights.metric: Pending order book (as on call date)
financial_highlights.change: New orders of INR538 crore booked in FY27 to date
US about INR50 crore, Africa (mainly Nigeria) about INR60 crore, balance Middle East (substantially ADNOC)

segments.name: Conventional oil and gas, fertilizer, thermal power
segments.commentary: Management said these businesses have strong traction and about INR1,000 crore of business is expected to continue from them for at least 10 years. Thermal power order intake exceeded INR150 crore.

segments.name: Air-cooled heat exchangers
segments.commentary: Execution started with an order from a German client; management described it as high-volume, moderate-margin (roughly 15%) work enabled by the Kheda facility.

segments.name: Technical services
segments.commentary: Management targets INR25 crore revenue in FY27, INR100 crore in FY28 and INR200 crore in the third year, at above 30% margin.

segments.name: Proprietary licensed / niche products
segments.commentary: Qualified for and won orders for two proprietary licensed products for export to process licensors; further niche wins targeted in the next three quarters.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth guided at 5% to 10%.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 15%, which management said reflects costs committed to projects under current conditions and may improve during execution.
Quarterly order intake expected at INR200 crore to INR250 crore per quarter.
Revenue recognition to be gradual from Q2, with Q3 and Q4 the highest revenue and EBITDA quarters.
Finance cost expected in Q2 FY27 to be about one-quarter of the Q1 level, per CFO.
Diversification into nuclear, hydrogen, green fertilizer and AI data-centre cooling targeted over roughly three years.
capex_capacity: Kheda facility, the bigger plant, is now fully operational and moving into complex equipment manufacturing with orders of about 12-month cycle.
Odhav used for heat exchangers; large ODC consignments cannot currently route via Strait of Hormuz, while smaller heat exchangers are being shipped by road to ADNOC.
Management said the entire order book for the year is full and the company is at capacity.
Raw material: mainly plates sourced from AM/NS ArcelorMittal and Jindal; 10-20% imported.
demand_pricing: Management said there is no current softness in demand; softness was seen for two quarters last year and is blamed for weak Q1 revenue.
Contracts are mostly fixed price; 99% of contracts are FOB India port, so freight is borne by the customer.
Recent order intake margins said to be close to historic margins over the last three to four months.
Management flagged risk of lower-tier competitors taking orders at lower margins, and said niche products are the response.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected order run-rate going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects order intake of INR200 crore to INR250 crore per quarter, supported by an inquiry pipeline of about INR1,100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Is the strategy shifting towards long-cycle products from high-volume, short-cycle work?
qa_highlights.answer: No; legacy complex products remain the core, niche products are a route to better win rates and margins, and high-volume items such as air-cooled heat exchangers (about 15% margin) continue alongside.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost rise, and are orders fixed price with raw material risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Finance cost moved with the cash position (cash-positive a year earlier, net cash about INR1 crore now); contracts are fixed price and the guidance includes current input costs, with no pass-through to customers.

qa_highlights.question: Is oil and gas demand softening, and what is the H2 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no softness; Q1 revenue was delayed by late execution start, with most due dates falling in H2, and Q3 and Q4 expected to be the strongest.

qa_highlights.question: Why not hedge raw material prices given a 6-8 week purchase lag?
qa_highlights.answer: Items are custom-made to order and designs need 4-6 weeks of customer approval before material is bought, so procurement is not commodity-style hedged.

qa_highlights.question: Export order book breakdown and logistics risk?
qa_highlights.answer: Export order book INR380 crore: about INR50 crore US, about INR60 crore Africa (mainly Nigeria), balance Middle East (mainly ADNOC). Large ODC consignments face Hormuz risk; smaller heat exchangers are going by road.

risks_watch: Revenue recognition depends on hitting project milestones; H2 weighting raises execution risk for the FY27 5-10% growth guidance.
Fixed-price contracts with elevated input and freight costs could pressure the about 15% EBITDA margin guidance.
Q1 EBITDA margin was low; management needs Q2-Q4 margins above 15% for the full-year average to hold.
Middle East shipping disruption (Strait of Hormuz) affects large ODC consignments.
Order intake must reach INR200-250 crore per quarter; Q1 order intake figure was not disclosed.
Lower-tier competitors may win orders at lower margins.
summary.management_tone: Management was candid about a weak Q1 and framed FY27 as a consolidation year, with guidance described as deliberately conservative. Confidence centred on the order book, the pipeline and the H2 ramp; management pushed back firmly on demand-softness questions. On raw material and freight, answers were direct but relied on contract terms rather than hedging detail.
key_quotes: This has been the best ever start for us on order book.
As of now, there is no softness in demand. In fact, it's a very robust demand, which is why there is confidence in the future.
we wish to provide a guidance for the year of a consolidated revenue growth of 5% to 10% and an EBITDA of about 15%.
Quarter 3 and quarter 4 is going to be the highest in terms of revenue generation and thereby EBITDA margins from that profile.

adds.what: Kheda facility (bigger plant) now fully operational, moving into complex equipment manufacturing

growth.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 5-10% (midpoint 7.5%) with EBITDA margin about 15%; backed by a pending order book of INR985 crore, INR538 crore of new FY27 orders, a 380 crore export book and a Kheda plant now fully operational, though no YoY quarterly comparison was given and revenue is back-end loaded.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at about 15% vs Q1 EBITDA of INR9.2 crore on INR125 crore revenue (about 7.4%), so Q2-Q4 must average above 15% for the year to hold; management said the 15% reflects committed costs and may improve during execution.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Kheda plant is now fully operational and management says the full-year order book is full and the company is at capacity, but no new capacity addition or timeline was given.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 5-10% (midpoint 7.5%) with revenue back-end loaded to Q3 and Q4, backed by a pending order book of INR985 crore and INR538 crore of new FY27 orders.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management says it is at capacity with the year's order book full, but no capex plan, land or approval was discussed on the call.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: FY27 revenue growth guided at 5-10% and EBITDA margin about 15%, described by management as deliberately conservative, but a Q1 revenue shortfall and H2 weighting leave little room for an early raise.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 revenue weighting depends on hitting project milestones, and fixed-price contracts with elevated input and freight costs could pressure the 15% margin guide.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Two proprietary licensed products already won for export to process licensors, with further niche wins targeted in the next three quarters; technical services targets INR25 crore revenue in FY27 and diversification into nuclear, hydrogen and AI data-centre cooling is set over about three years.

rows.label: Order intake of INR200-250 crore per quarter
rows.why: Guided at INR200-250 crore per quarter against INR538 crore booked in FY27 to date and an inquiry pipeline of about INR1,100 crore, though Q1 order intake was not disclosed.

rows.label: Export order book of INR380 crore
rows.why: Export book of INR380 crore (US about INR50 crore, Africa about INR60 crore, balance mainly ADNOC) with exports at about 50:50 of revenue, though large ODC consignments face Strait of Hormuz routing risk.

rows.label: Finance cost normalisation
rows.why: CFO expects Q2 FY27 finance cost at about one-quarter of Q1 level (Q1 at INR161 lakh, Q4 FY26 at INR221 lakh), tied to the net cash position of about INR1 crore.

tone.note: Management was candid that Q1 was weak and framed FY27 as a consolidation year with conservative guidance, confident on the order book, pipeline and H2 ramp; analysts pressed on the Q1 finance cost, demand softness, and fixed-price exposure to raw material and freight costs.
